segments.content:
Chapter 179 0176: A Korean Company Becomes Agent for Sanguosha (Extra Chapter for Alliance Leader An Shu Bo Luo)

"President Ren, hello!"

"Hello, CEO Chen."

As soon as the summit ended, Chen Guiliang immediately found Ren Yuxin. This man was currently the head of QQ Games and was about to become the Executive Vice President of Tencent Interactive Entertainment.

Fellow natives from Sichuan, the two started speaking directly in their local dialect.

"Lianzhong is still a behemoth. We need to join forces, and this is an opportunity," Chen Guiliang said.

Ren Yuxin nodded. "Indeed."

"We'll make our move today," Chen Guiliang said.

"I'll do my best," Ren Yuxin said.

After discussing a few more things, they each called their respective companies.

At noon that day, a news story appeared on the homepage of Tencent's portal, strongly condemning the Lianzhong representative for insulting the Chinese people. At the same time, users on Xiaonei and Kaixin began to spread what had happened that morning.

Beijing, Lianzhong Headquarters.

Bao Yueqiao, founder and CEO of Lianzhong, walked into Vice President Wu Guoliang's office with a face full of anger and slammed his hand on the desk. "See for yourself what that Korean has done. Does he even have a brain!"

"What happened?" Wu Guoliang was baffled.

He used to be the commercial director of Hong Kong Telecom and was recruited by Korea's NHN as the co-president for the China region, responsible for brokering the acquisition of Lianzhong.

Now, Wu Guoliang served as Lianzhong's CFO and Vice President.

To put it bluntly, he was there to help the Koreans control Lianzhong's finances, while also supervising Lianzhong's executives and coordinating between the Chinese and Korean staff.

Bao Yueqiao leaned over Wu Guoliang's computer, quickly found Tencent's website, and clicked on it. "Look, look what he's done. Even a primary school student wouldn't do something like this!"

Wu Guoliang carefully read the Tencent news article and took a deep breath. "I can't understand it either."

"No normal person could understand it. I even suspect he was cursed or something!" Bao Yueqiao was so angry his facial muscles trembled.

Wu Guoliang said, "Let's contact a few media outlets. We'll say the Korean isn't fluent in Chinese, that he didn't mean it that way, and that his expression was just ambiguous."

"Who do you think will believe that?" Bao Yueqiao asked.

"We have to find some way to save face," Wu Guoliang said.

Bao Yueqiao said, "I'm going to contact the Korean side. These dozens of Koreans who came to China are good for nothing but causing trouble. I demand that all of them be withdrawn!"

"If one batch is withdrawn, a new one will just come," Wu Guoliang reminded him.

Bao Yueqiao was seething with rage. "I don't care. This bastard must get out of Lianzhong!"

Wu Guoliang said, "I can only help you make contact."

"Immediately!"

Bao Yueqiao couldn't wait another minute.

Wu Guoliang had no choice but to call NHN headquarters, rattling off in English. He hung up and said, "NHN will recall Park Heon-joo to Korea for questioning."

"Just questioning?" Bao Yueqiao said, dissatisfied.

Wu Guoliang nodded. "Yes."

"Son of a bitch!" Bao Yueqiao stormed out.

Lianzhong originally had three founders. The other two had already been forced out, leaving Bao Yueqiao to hold the fort alone.

Early last year, NHN invested 100 million USD to acquire a 50% stake in Lianzhong. The three founders each received 14 million USD in cash.

At the time, they were quite happy. Lianzhong had long been controlled by Hanhong Holdings, which wasn't very professional when it came to gaming. The Korean company NHN, on the other hand, was very professional. With the support of a Korean company and 100 million USD in funding, Lianzhong was sure to develop rapidly and forge ahead.

But they were soon dumbfounded. NHN parachuted in dozens of Koreans who directly took over Lianzhong's middle management positions.

Most of those guys couldn't speak Chinese, making daily communication extremely difficult, and they would pull bizarre stunts from time to time. They even forced Chinese employees who made mistakes to kneel!

In just over a year, a large number of Lianzhong's core employees had resigned, and even two of the founders had left.

Sitting in his office, Bao Yueqiao chain-smoked one cigarette after another.

He had already made up his mind. If this batch of Koreans was withdrawn only to be replaced by another batch of brain-dead ones, he would also resign as CEO of Lianzhong.

*I'm done with this.*

He had already cashed out over 10 million USD anyway. At worst, he could start a second venture in another field.

His two former partners had both started their own companies after leaving Lianzhong. Weren't they doing quite well? And they didn't have to put up with any crap from the Koreans!

Clicking on the Tencent news article again, Bao Yueqiao looked as if he were wearing a mask of pain. How could there be such a stupid person in this world?

"I find it hard to understand how there can be such a person."

Chen Guiliang was in the middle of an exclusive interview with 17173.

He was speaking the truth. He really couldn't understand it. It was as if the other party had been hit with an intelligence-lowering spell.

"None of us have any grudge against him. What he said brought no benefit to himself or to Lianzhong. After thinking it over, there's only one possibility."

"What's the reason?"

"Those were his true thoughts, and he blurted them out without any reservation. He genuinely thinks Chinese people are fools."

"So Youke really won't be an agent for Korean games in the future?"

"I'm a man of my word."

"A while ago, it seems ByteDance acquired a startup game company."

"Yes. This game company is very popular on your 17173 forums."

"Do you think this company's game can succeed?"

"I've personally tried it. I believe it can succeed."

"What are Youke's future plans?"

"Of course, it's to first do a good job with Sanguosha..."

The afternoon's activities consisted of various press conferences and signing ceremonies.

Both standalone and online games took the opportunity to make an appearance at the expo. Major international companies like EA and Sony, as well as some Korean companies, also came to showcase their products.

The representatives of several Korean game developers sat together chatting after lunch.

"Did you guys hear? A guy NHN sent to China misspoke at the summit and has caused a public outrage."

"That guy is so stupid. Even if it's the truth, you can't say it in public."

"If he's from NHN, I wouldn't be surprised by anything he does."

"I really hope NHN goes bankrupt."

Although these Korean developer representatives weren't siding with the Chinese, they were still mocking and even cursing NHN.

Because in the Korean internet industry, NHN was also a universally loathed entity.

It owned Korea's largest portal site, largest search engine, and largest casual games platform, as well as its own blog and online community.

For several years now, NHN has been using its search engine monopoly to maliciously lower the search rankings of its competitors. Anyone whose business competed with NHN's would face search suppression.

Chen Guiliang's Youke Interactive platform had agreed to help sell *Blade & Sword*, taking a 25% cut from the developer.

NHN's game platform also sold games from other companies. What was the platform's cut?

Over 80%!

You heard that right, 80% for the platform.

They already had a monopoly on the Korean game platform market. Your only options were yes or no.

NHN also loved to acquire emerging game companies, only to forcibly dissolve them after the acquisition.

When shutting down a game, they never issued refunds or even gave users advance notice.

And within the company, the 996 work culture was truly a blessing for NHN's programmers. They went straight for 007, with average weekly working hours exceeding 80. If you died from exhaustion, it was considered voluntary overtime.

Park Heon-joo was a complete nobody at NHN headquarters, constantly in a state of depression. The moment he arrived in China, he completely let himself go.

Among this group of Koreans complaining about NHN, one of them walked straight towards Youke's booth.

Today was only open to industry professionals and the media; the general public had to wait until tomorrow to enter. As a result, there weren't many people at the Youke booth. Most had gone to see *World of Warcraft*.

Several agents from mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan were currently playing *Sanguosha*. A new character card pack had just been released a few days ago.

"Does anyone here speak English or Korean?" Shin Yoo-bin asked a staff member at the Youke booth in English.

Someone immediately came over to shake his hand. "Hello, I speak English."

Shin Yoo-bin said, "I am a representative of Renticsoftware from Korea. We specialize in bringing overseas games into the Korean market. We were the agent for the Korean version of *JX Online*."

In Korea at that time, there were indeed companies that acted as agents for Chinese games.

Not only did *JX Online* have a Korean version, so did *Blade & Sword Online*. However, due to poor localization and overly fierce market competition, both games had failed in Korea.

Shin Yoo-bin said, "Please explain the gameplay of this game to me."

The staff member said, "This is a card game. There are identity cards, character cards, tool cards... The current Monarch is Guo Jia. The Da Qiao in the eighth position is very likely a Rebel, because Da Qiao's ability is..."

The more Shin Yoo-bin listened, the more interested he became. In the current Korean online game market, the competition among MMORPGs was too intense. *Lineage II* was crushing all other games.

Last year, they had brought *JX Online* to Korea, only to be obliterated by *Lineage II*.

They could take a completely different path and introduce *Sanguosha* to Korea, avoiding direct competition with *Lineage II*.

The representative from Taiwan's Soft-World International Corporation stood up after playing a few rounds and said to a staff member, "I'm interested in being the agent for *Sanguosha*, both the online game and the physical cards. Who do I speak to?"

"This way, please," the staff member said with a smile.

Shin Yoo-bin immediately grabbed the empty seat and said, "I'd like to play it myself."

The English-speaking staff member said, "Click here to enter a room, here to get ready for battle... Now you're in the game. Your identity is Turncoat. This account is a premium member, so you have five character choices. You can pick one of them... Dian Wei's ability is... Sun Shangxiang's ability is... Time is running out, just pick Sun Quan..."

After playing three consecutive games, Shin Yoo-bin remained seated, unwilling to give up his spot. He asked, "How do you charge for this?"

The staff member said, "First, there's a paid membership. A basic membership gives you one extra character choice, and a premium membership gives you two, plus more experience points and silver than regular users, as well as other consumable items. See this user avatar? We call it a Sanguo Show. Premium Sanguo Shows must be purchased... These characters also have different skins..."

Shin Yoo-bin listened intently. He had already decided to bring *Sanguosha* to Korea.

The staff member brought over a box. "These are the physical *Sanguosha* cards. You can also play with friends offline."

"The production quality is very exquisite," Shin Yoo-bin said. "Who is your person in charge of negotiations?"

"This way, please."

(End of Chapter)
